description:
## What

In `src/fetcher/dns_cache.cr`, `ensure_cleanup_registered` reads-then-writes `@@cleanup_registered` without holding `@@lock`. The OLD code got away with this because the only caller was inside the lock. Now that `CrestHttpClient.ensure_dns_cleanup_registered` exposes it as a public shim, two concurrent external shim calls can both pass the `return if @@cleanup_registered` check and both call `PeriodicCleanup.register_cleanup` — registering duplicate procs (the `Set` de-dups by identity, but each call passes a fresh proc literal).

## Why

Pre-existing race, exposed by the 9el.1 refactor. Self-locking fixes it without changing the public API.

## How

In `dns_cache.cr`, split into an internal unlocked helper + a public locked wrapper:

```crystal
private def self.ensure_cleanup_registered_unlocked : Nil
  return if @@cleanup_registered
  @@cleanup_registered = true
  PeriodicCleanup.register_cleanup { clear_expired }
end

# Public wrapper. Takes the lock so external shim callers are safe.
# Note: store() also calls this helper directly under @@lock, which is why
# the unlocked variant exists — Crystal Mutex is not re-entrant.
def self.ensure_cleanup_registered : Nil
  @@lock.synchronize { ensure_cleanup_registered_unlocked }
end
```

Update `store` to call the unlocked variant.

## Done when

- `@@cleanup_registered` write is always under `@@lock`
- `store` still works (uses unlocked variant)
- Public shim `CrestHttpClient.ensure_dns_cleanup_registered` is concurrency-safe
- Full spec suite still green (415 examples)
title: Refactor: make DnsCache.ensure_cleanup_registered self-locking (9el.1 follow-up)
